sections.heading: What Causes Foggy Windows and Why Prompt Repair Matters
sections.body: Foggy windows occur when the airtight seal surrounding an insulated glass unit breaks down. Double- and triple-pane windows are filled with insulating gas, typically argon or krypton, and when the perimeter seal fails, outside air and humidity infiltrate the gap between the panes. The result is condensation, streaking, and a permanent cloudy appearance that no amount of cleaning can fix from the outside. Beyond the cosmetic issue, a broken seal means your window is no longer performing its insulating function. Heat escapes in winter and enters in summer, forcing your HVAC system to work harder and driving up energy bills. In a busy commercial property or a residential home in Arlington, this inefficiency adds up quickly. Addressing the problem early by replacing only the failed insulated glass unit, rather than the entire window frame, saves significant money and minimizes disruption to your daily operations or home life.

faq.q: Can foggy windows be repaired without replacing the entire window frame?
faq.a: Yes. In most cases, only the insulated glass unit needs to be replaced, not the entire window frame. Our technicians remove the failed pane, install a new precision-matched insulated glass unit, and reseal it within the existing frame, saving you significant cost compared to a full window replacement.

faq.q: How long does foggy window repair take in Arlington?
faq.a: Most residential foggy window repairs are completed in a single visit, often within a few hours depending on the number of windows and glass unit availability. Commercial projects with multiple affected windows may be scheduled in phases. We provide a clear timeline during your initial estimate.

faq.q: Does foggy window repair improve energy efficiency?
faq.a: Absolutely. A failed seal means your window is no longer providing proper insulation. Replacing the insulated glass unit restores the argon or krypton gas fill and thermal barrier, which reduces heat transfer, improves indoor comfort, and lowers your heating and cooling costs.
